newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Ceylon Tobacco says drought, smuggling hit profit.
newsitem.headline: Ceylon Tobacco says drought, smuggling hit profit.

text.p: Sri Lanka's Ceylon Tobacco Co Ltd, a subsidiary of BAT Industries Plc said profits in the first quarter of 1997 were hit mostly by a drought and cigarette smuggling.
Sri Lanka's monopoly cigarette-maker said net profit for the first quarter ending March 31, 1997 fell 4.3 percent to 101.74 million rupees on turnover of 4.29 billion rupees.
"A drought in the beginning of the year and then the impact from smuggled cigarettes affected net profit in the first quarter of 1997," a company spokesman told Reuters on Tuesday.
He said the drought had reduced the purchasing power of consumers, most of whom live in rural areas. Over 80 percent of Sri Lanka's population of 18 million people live in rural areas.

Smuggled cigarettes which have long plagued Ceylon Tobacco, continue to hamper profit growth, the spokesman said. Studies show that Sri Lanka's annual consumption of cigarettes is around 5.5 billion sticks. Smuggled cigarettes are estimated to account for a further 240 million sticks.
Ceylon Tobacco's revenue could rise by one billion rupees if smuggling is rooted out, said a recent research report by UBS Keells.
The report said low debt combined with cost rationalistation and lower taxation, should see profits rise by about 12 prcent to 642 million rupees in the current 1997 (Jan-Dec) financial year.
